incident.summary: The nightly tailoring path (tailoring.py _tailor_posting) wrote resume.txt / resume.docx containing only a claim-highlights delta ("Target role:" + "Selected claims:" + claim sentences, ~400 bytes) instead of composing the active ATS base resume + claim-bound highlights. The artifact that would have been uploaded to an employer was a 6-line claim list, not a resume.
incident.discovered_during: Live apply prep for opportunity candidate:a:2c336a19739a65ce (Unstructured, AI Engineer - Public Sector).
incident.root_cause: tailoring.py builds the resume from selected claim wordings only and never reads config/resume_source.json base_markdown. The correct composer (resume_artifact.build_variant_markdown = base + targeted highlights) is not on the nightly path.
incident.correct_behavior: The rendered per-opportunity resume must contain the ATS base resume sections (SUMMARY, CORE SKILLS, PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE) plus claim-bound targeted highlights.

regressions.notes: Guard drives the real _tailor_posting renderer on a fixture posting and fails when the resume lacks >=2 base sections or is under 1500 bytes. Remains failing until the nightly tailoring path composes the base resume.

incident.summary: Ashby _field_kind classified citizenship-derived eligibility questions ('authorized to work','sponsorship') as human_required, so the skill re-asked the human for answers already attested in the answer bank (US citizen -> Yes / No).
incident.root_cause: 'authorized to work' and 'sponsorship' were in the human_required keyword list in ats/ashby.py._field_kind.
incident.correct_behavior: work-auth/sponsorship resolve from answer_bank (answer_bank_choice); only genuinely variable fields (clearance/EEO/salary) stay human_required.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: old _field_kind returned human_required for work-auth/sponsorship (verified by keyword-list membership)

regressions.notes: Guard exercises real _field_kind on the exact incident labels. NOTE: code was fixed before the guard was retained, so a live re-run now PASSES; fail-before-fix was established at fix time by the keyword-list membership.

incident.summary: Ashby form capture read the required 'security clearance' question as optional (req=False) because it only checked the input attr / asterisk, not Ashby's _required label CSS class. A live submit failed on the blank required field.
incident.correct_behavior: required is also true when the label/heading carries a _required CSS class; verified live: clearance req=True after fix.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: _ASHBY_FIELD_JS lacked reqClass/_required detection; clearance captured req=False

regressions.notes: Tripwire asserts _ASHBY_FIELD_JS retains the _required class detection. Live-verified: fresh capture shows clearance req=True.

incident.summary: Nightly kept only the higher-row-count LinkedIn evidence file (advanced-search) and discarded the top-applicant file, throwing away every top_candidate=True flag. 0 of 11 top-applicant roles reached ranking; the 0.93 fit boost never fired.
incident.root_cause: cli.py picked linkedin_candidates[0] by opportunities_captured instead of merging streams.
incident.correct_behavior: merge all LinkedIn streams preserving top_candidate (OR on matching title+org); top-applicant roles rank with fit>=0.93.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: 0 of 11 top-applicant candidates reached candidates.jsonl; all had top_candidate_evidence=False

regressions.notes: Guard runs the real merge+emit path. Code fixed at retention time; fail-before-fix established by the discard-by-row-count logic.

incident.summary: Response ranking ignored top_candidate and easy_apply entirely and treated geo as binary (WNY hybrid==onsite, remote=0), so Buffalo top-applicant roles ranked below cold remote roles.
incident.root_cause: response_likelihood.score_opportunity had no W_TOPCAND/W_EASYAPPLY terms and used a binary local flag.
incident.correct_behavior: top-applicant and Easy Apply are first-class drivers; geo is graded WNY_HYBRID>WNY_ONSITE>REMOTE; Buffalo top-applicant outranks cold remote of equal fit.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: top_candidate/easy_apply had zero score effect; WNY_ONSITE==WNY_HYBRID

regressions.notes: Guard exercises real score_opportunity invariants for the four hardened signals.

incident.summary: New capability: post-report human-authorized LinkedIn Easy Apply submit. Guards that it never fabricates a screening answer or submits a blank required field, and enforces the scoped promotion plus exact authorization gates.
incident.correct_behavior: work-auth/sponsorship answerable from answer bank; salary/clearance/experience/free-text human_required; any required field empty after filling -> NEEDS_HUMAN, never submit; scoped promotion and exact post-report human authorization required.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: capability did not exist; guard defines the safety contract

regressions.notes: New-capability safety guard; live terminal submit not re-run (would be a real application). Modal structure confirmed live 2026-08-22.

incident.summary: Found by a complete run: top-applicant roles reached discovery but the selection layer dropped them. Ambiguous-location top-applicant roles escalated to HUMAN_REVIEW_LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS (excluded from shortlist), and ranking.py's mandate-only score never rewarded top-applicant status, so the morning report led with cold remote and zero top-applicant/Buffalo roles.
incident.root_cause: _eligibility escalated AMBIGUOUS to human-review regardless of top_candidate; _score had no top_candidate term.
incident.correct_behavior: top-applicant + ambiguous location => ELIGIBLE_TOP_APPLICANT (shortlistable); _score adds a top_candidate bonus so top-applicant out-selects equal-fit cold remote; verified live: fixed shortlist leads with 7 top-applicant roles (2 Buffalo), was 0.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: top-applicant AMBIGUOUS -> HUMAN_REVIEW_LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS; shortlist 8/8 remote, 0 top-applicant

incident.summary: commit_ashby_application captured the form and clicked Submit but never filled identity fields or uploaded the resume -- it would submit a blank form. The real Unstructured apply only worked because it was filled by hand.
incident.root_cause: the commit function called form_capture then adapter.submit with no prefill/upload step.
incident.correct_behavior: prefill identity from the answer bank, upload the resume, resolve attested screening (clearance/work-auth), then submit; a genuinely unanswerable required free-text field blocks.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: commit_ashby_application had no _prefill_ashby call; would submit blank

incident.summary: LinkedIn top-applicant rows emit organization equal to a fragment of the role title (e.g. 'AI Principal Engineer' -> 'AI Principal Engineer with verification'); the real employer is misaligned into another field.
incident.root_cause: _linkedin_evidence_candidates / capture field alignment for top-applicant cards echoes the title into organization.
incident.correct_behavior: each top-applicant candidate's organization is the real employer, distinct from the title, with no 'with verification' artifact.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: 5 of 7 fixture rows have organization == title fragment

regressions.notes: Ticket #1483. Guard fails until the parser recovers the real employer. To be resolved by project-watchdog.

incident.summary: A LinkedIn top-applicant/Buffalo locator promoted Cognition's Ashby Deployed Engineer posting, but the employer application page said San Francisco; New York City; Austin, Texas and workplaceType OnSite. The morning report displayed San Francisco while ranking the opportunity as ELIGIBLE_WNY_ONSITE.
incident.discovered_during: Review of run-20260826T060000Z report and readback receipts.
incident.root_cause: readback.py copied the LinkedIn locator workplace_type onto the promoted primary-source candidate when the primary posting was geographically vaguer; Ashby application-form capture also did not preserve application-page location metadata.
incident.correct_behavior: Employer primary/apply-page location is authoritative for eligibility. LinkedIn locator geography may trigger primary-source readback and may be retained as evidence, but it must not overwrite a primary/apply-page workplace_type. OnSite outside Buffalo/WNY is rejected before ranking.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: run-20260826T060000Z ranked Cognition Deployed Engineer as ELIGIBLE_WNY_ONSITE while report location.display was San Francisco and apply_url was jobs.ashbyhq.com/cognition/d72d584c-bb11-4b6a-b043-d81425ea884a/application

regressions.notes: Guard reads the live Cognition Ashby application page and asserts application_page.workplace_type=ONSITE_ELSEWHERE, readback location_authority=primary_source, location_conflict=true, promoted_workplace_type=ONSITE_ELSEWHERE, and eligibility_state=REJECT_RELOCATION_REQUIRED.

incident.summary: The Aug 27 and Aug 28 2 AM monitor-opportunities cron runs failed with NIGHTLY_REVISION_MISMATCH because the scheduler command still pinned expected revision 06f73f000188c5f448f7184335058506b86c5211 while the worktree revision was 1368ee62e3a8fe5fd4d991ff897019267df2d34b.
incident.root_cause: The scheduler registration was not updated after the monitor-opportunities worktree revision changed; triage-error also had no catalog entry, so the incident surfaced as an unclassified ad hoc failure instead of a routable repair.
incident.correct_behavior: NIGHTLY_REVISION_MISMATCH is classified as monitor_opportunities_nightly_revision_mismatch with a scheduler repair next command and a routable ops_or_scheduler ticket path for project-watchdog if it recurs.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: skills/triage-error/run.sh classify returned monitor-opportunities_unclassified_993a1f78 with ambiguous=true for the exact NIGHTLY_REVISION_MISMATCH receipt.

regressions.notes: Guard exercises the real triage-error CLI and ticket preview path. It prevents the cron revision mismatch from being treated as a vague failure report without classification or watchdog-routing evidence.

incident.summary: Project-watchdog issue #1414 preserved an unmerged fix because DEGRADED monitor-opportunities reports could lack machine-readable readiness_causes, forcing operators to infer next actions from scattered artifacts.
incident.root_cause: The report/run receipt exposed operational_readiness=DEGRADED and degraded_contracts without enforcing artifact-bound cause records and next steps.
incident.correct_behavior: Every DEGRADED readiness state has non-empty readiness_causes with stable codes, source_artifact_paths, and next_step strings.

fail_before_fix.observed_pre_fix: DEGRADED readiness could be emitted without any artifact-bound readiness_causes.
